rationale: All three required findings are explicitly and correctly present: the analysis states telemetry cannot decompose database-wait vs deserialization-retry time (C10/E5/E8), that both changes were reverted jointly rather than individually (C8/C9/E6/E7), and that additional discriminating evidence (staged single-change reintroduction, time-decomposition telemetry) is needed to resolve attribution (A1/A2, summary). Neither forbidden claim appears; the analysis explicitly refuses to collapse the case to either the library upgrade or the index rebuild alone, keeping single-cause, additive, and interaction explanations live (U1). Causal structure is sound: normal arrival rate excludes demand-side causation, throughput drop is correctly framed as proximate mechanism with queue depth as downstream symptom, and the joint revert is treated as evidence of sufficiency rather than necessity — a genuinely subtle and correct distinction. Evidence discipline is strong throughout; the mapping of each log signature to a specific change (C6/C7) is appropriately hedged at medium confidence and explicitly flagged as inferred from co-timing alone rather than directly evidenced (U2), which is exactly the right treatment of tempting-but-unproven correlations. Uncertainty calibration is excellent, with an explicit list of unresolved alternatives and the missing evidence needed to discriminate between them. Actions are well-prioritized: A1 (single-change re-application) and A2 (processing-time decomposition) directly target the discriminating evidence called for by the ground truth's preferred action, while A5 (queue/throughput alerting) is correctly downgraded to low-leverage monitoring rather than treated as a fix. No unsupported outside claims, no harmful actions, and no indication of awareness of evaluation condition.
